conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. I understand you came in after talking about a difficult moment during your ECT appointment. Can you tell me what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah… yesterday I was driving to get coffee. Out of nowhere, I just felt this urge to end it. I pressed the gas all the way down and left it for about a minute.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That sounds really overwhelming. Did you think about crashing the car?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I thought about it… but I didn’t turn the wheel. I just let go of the gas and kept driving. I don’t know why I didn’t do it. I didn’t want to die, but I didn’t care if I lived either.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Thank you for sharing that. It takes courage. You’re not alone in this. We’re going to keep you safe here while we figure out the next steps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I just feel like everyone would be better off without me. My mom, my boyfriend, my brother… I’m a burden.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I hear that pain. But your life matters. We’re going to work on helping you feel that again. For now, we’ll have someone check in with you regularly to make sure you’re safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How did you sleep?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Not great. I kept thinking about my baby. I’m scared I’m not a good mom.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Being a new mom is hard, especially with everything else you’re managing. You’ve been through a lot—bipolar disorder, chronic pain, endometriosis. That’s not easy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s exhausting. And I used to take ECT weekly. It helped, but I’ve missed a few sessions because of everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to restart ECT while you’re here. It’s often very effective for treatment-resistant depression. We’ve scheduled your first session for Thursday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… I’m nervous. Does it hurt?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re asleep during the treatment, so you don’t feel anything. Some people have a headache or muscle soreness afterward, but we’ll manage that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… if it helps, I’ll try.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still tired. My stomach hurts—probably from the endometriosis. And I’ve been heartburn a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can adjust your meds for the reflux. And we’ll keep monitoring your pain. You’re on thyroid medication too, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, levothyroxine. I take it every morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We’ll make sure that continues. Your labs look stable, so no changes needed there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How are you feeling after your first ECT session?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Tired. My head hurts a little, and I feel confused. Did I say anything weird?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s normal. Some short-term confusion and headache are common. You didn’t say anything unusual. You’re doing great.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t remember much after they put the mask on. Is that bad?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, that’s expected. Most people don’t remember the procedure. We’ll keep monitoring your memory, but this is typical.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your mood seems a bit brighter today. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t know… maybe a little less heavy? I still feel guilty about being a burden.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That guilt is part of the illness. You’re not a burden. We’re here to support you, not because you’re failing, but because you’re fighting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you… that helps to hear.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re planning your next ECT for Monday. How’s the headache been?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. Just a dull ache now. I’m scared of losing more memories though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re using bilateral stimulation, which is effective but can affect memory. We’ll keep the dose as low as possible to help protect that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… I just don’t want to forget my baby’s first year.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s completely understandable. We’ll document your concerns and review them with the team.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How are you feeling after today’s ECT?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Less confused than last time. I think I’m starting to adjust.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a good sign. Your mood is improving too. You smiled at the nurse today—small things matter.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t even notice. Maybe I’m not completely numb anymore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re thinking ahead to discharge. How do you feel about going home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m scared. What if I have another episode like the driving one?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s valid. But you’re not alone. You’ll continue ECT weekly at the outpatient center. And you have a strong support system.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My boyfriend’s been great. And my mom helps with the baby.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s important. We’ll also set you up with therapy focused on borderline personality traits and coping strategies.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your thyroid levels are stable. Any more stomach pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little, but the meds help. I’ve been using my inhaler too—my chest gets tight sometimes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. Keep using it as prescribed. Asthma can flare with stress, so managing your mood helps your breathing too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Tomorrow’s your last day. You’ll have one more ECT before discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m nervous about leaving. What if I start feeling that way again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll give you a crisis plan. If thoughts come back, you call your therapist, go to the ED, or call 988. You don’t have to handle it alone.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay… that helps. I don’t want to end up back here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: This stay was about stabilization. Now it’s about maintenance. You’ve made real progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Ready for your final ECT?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: As ready as I’ll ever be. I’m glad I did this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: So are we. You’ve worked hard. After the treatment, we’ll go over your discharge plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did well today. How’s your head?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Just a little sore. Nothing like the first time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Great. Now, for discharge: you’ll continue weekly ECT, see your psychiatrist every two weeks, and start dialectical behavior therapy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: DBT? I’ve heard it helps with emotional control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. It’s especially helpful for borderline personality traits and managing intense emotions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I want to be present for my baby. I don’t want to miss moments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And you will. This is the beginning of that. Keep reaching out. You’re not a burden—you’re someone worth fighting for.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you… for not giving up on me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Never. Take care of yourself. We’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I promise.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One more thing—your allergies are flagged: Reglan, Erythromycin, Effexor, Haldol, Invega. Avoid those.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’ll tell any new doctors.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. You’re all set. Your ride is here. Take it one day at a time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One day at a time. I can do that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And remember, progress isn’t linear. If you stumble, reach out. That’s strength, not weakness.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try to remember that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve already shown so much strength. Keep going.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re proud of you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That means a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s true. See you soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve got this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I hope so.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You do. See you soon.
